title: What "8000W" Really Means on a Blender in Ghana
excerpt: Almost every blender sold in Ghana claims 4500W or 8000W. On a Ghanaian socket, both numbers are physically impossible. Here is the arithmetic, and the real number.
content:
Quick answer. No blender plugged into a Ghanaian wall socket can draw 8000W, or 4500W. A Type G socket delivers at most 2,990W and a Type D at most 1,380W. The number on the box is a peak marketing figure. Real continuous draw on a typical 2L commercial blender is around 600W, which costs about GHS 6.11 a month to run.

The arithmetic anyone can check

Ghana's mains supply is 230 volts. Power is volts multiplied by amps. The two domestic socket types set a hard ceiling:

SocketRated ampsMaximum deliverable power
Type G (the rectangular three pin)13A230 x 13 = 2,990W
Type D (the round three pin)6A230 x 6 = 1,380W

An 8000W load would need 34.8 amps, which is 2.7 times what a Type G socket can supply and 5.8 times a Type D. The fuse in the plug blows long before the motor ever sees that power. A 4500W claim needs 19.6 amps and fails the same test.

So why is the number on the box?

It is a peak or stall figure: the instantaneous surge at motor startup, or the theoretical maximum the windings could momentarily survive. It is not what the motor draws while blending your pepper. The same trick inflates horsepower claims on premium blender brands worldwide. One horsepower is 746 watts, so treat these labels as marketing units rather than electrical ones.

What it actually costs you to run

At the PURC residential rate of GHS 2.04 per kWh, effective 1 July 2026, ten minutes of blending a day comes to:

Real continuous drawkWh per monthCost per month
300W1.5GHS 3.06
600W (typical 2L commercial)3.0GHS 6.11
800W4.0GHS 8.15
1200W6.0GHS 12.23

Here is the part that should change how you shop: the blender, the appliance with the scariest number on the box, is one of the cheapest things in your kitchen to run. The quiet ones are the expensive ones. A double burner hot plate at typical use costs about GHS 91.69 a month.

What to look at instead of the wattage

Jar size for your family, whether it comes with a genuine dry mill if you grind grains and spices, blade metal, and whether the seller holds local stock so a warranty claim has somewhere to go. Every blender we sell states its realistic draw class, its running cost at the current tariff, and its price verified for the current month.

Sources and working: PURC Q2 2026 tariff decision plus the 3.49 per cent increase effective 1 July 2026; Ghana mains 230V; socket ratings per the Type G (13A) and Type D (6A) standards. Cost formula: watts / 1000 x hours per day x 30 x rate.

title: What 30,000mAh Really Delivers to Your Phone
excerpt: A power bank never delivers its advertised mAh. The physics is settled and the arithmetic is simple. Here is the real number, and how many charges you actually get.
content:
Quick answer. A "30,000mAh" power bank delivers roughly 15,500 to 18,900mAh to your phone, about three to four full charges of a typical 5,000mAh battery, not six. This is true of every brand at every price. The cells store charge at 3.7 volts, your phone receives it at 5 volts, and the conversion between them loses energy as heat.

The formula

Energy is conserved in watt hours, not milliamp hours. The advertised mAh is measured at the cell voltage, and delivery happens at USB voltage:

Real mAh at 5V = (3.7 x advertised mAh x efficiency) / 5.0

Quality units convert at about 85 per cent efficiency. Budget units, which is most of what sells in Accra, run nearer 70 per cent.

AdvertisedStored energyReal at 5V (budget)Real at 5V (quality)
10,000mAh37.0 Wh5,180mAh6,290mAh
20,000mAh74.0 Wh10,360mAh12,580mAh
30,000mAh111.0 Wh15,540mAh18,870mAh

The industry already admits this

Anker publishes the same arithmetic for its own products, quoting roughly 82 per cent efficiency and a "rated capacity" near 6,068mAh on a 10,000mAh bank. The information is not hidden. It is just never said at the point of sale in Ghana.

How many charges you actually get

Divide the real delivered figure by your phone's battery. A 5,000mAh phone gets about one full charge from a 10,000mAh bank, two from a 20,000mAh, and three to four from a 30,000mAh. If a listing promises six charges from 30,000mAh, the seller has not done the arithmetic, or hopes you will not.

One more thing before you fly

Airlines generally cap carry-on batteries at 100Wh without approval. A 30,000mAh unit stores about 111Wh, over that line. Up to 20,000mAh (74Wh) travels without questions.

Why we tell you this

Because you already know your power bank underdelivers. You have owned one. We would rather be the shop that explains why, with the working on the page, than the fifth listing shouting a number physics does not permit. Every power bank we sell states its honest charge count, and its price is verified for the current month.
